free_tier.stated: 1 TiB of free DataCap per verified client, instantly, via Gitcoin Passport (score >= 20) on Optimism. Fil+ allocators can grant more. DataCap is a one-time, non-transferable credit. 'If a client needs more DataCap, they must request additional allocations.'.

egress.terms: Not free, and this is what kills it. DataCap buys storage deal quality, not bandwidth. On Filecoin Onchain Cloud the retrieval layer is Filecoin Beam: 'Up to $14/TiB (≈ $0.014/GiB) egress'. FCSS: 'Retrieval is billed per TiB retrieved, with one free full-dataset retrieval a year'; unsealed HTTP retrieval returns 402 Payment Required per paid piece.

record.tooling: Lotus/Boost deal-making, Singularity (github.com/data-preservation-programs/singularity), Spade for renewals, synapse-sdk for FOC, retrieval-client for FCSS.
record.chaining: DataCap is per verified client and explicitly non-transferable; GLIF Verify caps re-verification at once per 30 days and grants from 64 GiB by GitHub account age. Multiple Gitcoin Passports are an identity-farming exercise, not a technical multiplier. And even a successful farm buys storage, not egress.
record.limits_note: 64 GiB+ via GLIF (GitHub age dependent), 1 TiB via the faucet; deal duration fixed at signing; retrieval metered; FCSS minimum 6-month term.
record.reliability_note: DataCap grants verified storage deals up to 1 TiB of storage capacity. Data retrieval and egress are metered separately by storage providers.
